A.explanation: This is only the thinking distance, the rectangle $20 \times 0.8 = 16 \text{ m}$, and omits the distance travelled while braking from $0.8 \text{ s}$ to $5.0 \text{ s}$.

B.explanation: This is only the braking distance, the triangle $0.5 \times 20 \times 4.2 = 42 \text{ m}$, and omits the $16 \text{ m}$ travelled at constant $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ before braking.

C.explanation: This is the total area under the velocity-time graph from $0$ to $5.0 \text{ s}$, $16 \text{ m} + 42 \text{ m} = 58 \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: This treats the braking phase as a rectangle $20 \times 4.2 = 84 \text{ m}$ instead of a triangle, ignoring that velocity falls linearly to zero.

hints: Notice the graph stays flat at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 0.8 \text{ s}$, then slopes down to zero at $t = 5.0 \text{ s}$.
Recall that distance travelled equals the area under a velocity-time graph, so split this shape into a rectangle plus a triangle.
Calculate $20 \times 0.8$ for the first part and $0.5 \times 20 \times (5.0 - 0.8)$ for the second part, then add them.
walkthrough: Identify the two motions: constant velocity $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ for $0.8 \text{ s}$ of reaction time, then uniform deceleration to rest between $0.8 \text{ s}$ and $5.0 \text{ s}$.
Use distance = area under the velocity-time graph. The first part is a rectangle of height $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and width $0.8 \text{ s}$.
Rectangle area = $20 \times 0.8 = 16 \text{ m}$. This is the thinking distance.
The second part is a triangle of height $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and base $5.0 - 0.8 = 4.2 \text{ s}$.
Triangle area = $0.5 \times 20 \times 4.2 = 42 \text{ m}$. This is the braking distance.
Total distance = $16 + 42 = 58 \text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$. This is option C.
